heroIntro: Tell us what the system is doing and where you are. We share it with the HVAC company or companies covering your part of Houston, and you get a call back with a next step.
intro: Most AC problems in Houston are not mystery failures. They are a condenser packed with cottonwood, a system that was undersized for a house that got an addition, a coil that froze because the filter had not been changed since spring. Somebody who works that street every day recognises it faster than a call center script does, which is why we ask for your area before we send the request anywhere.
whyRequest: We send it to a company that already works your area
You describe the symptom in your own words, no ticket number
You get a call back with a next step, not a survey
Nothing costs you anything, the company pays for the referral
You are under no obligation to go ahead with the work

steps.d: What the system is doing, when it started, what you have already tried. Three lines is usually enough for a technician to know roughly where to look.

steps.t: We find the companies that cover your street
steps.d: We share it with the HVAC companies working your part of Houston, so the person coming out already knows the housing stock and the weather.
You get a person on the phone who can ask the questions a form cannot, and tell you what the options and the costs look like before anyone turns a wrench.
The quote and the work are between you and that company. There is nothing on this site that obliges you to accept either one.

faqs.q: Is it free to request AC service?
faqs.a: Yes, and it stays free. The HVAC company or companies that take your request pay us a referral fee, and that fee never gets passed to you. Nothing on this site charges you for anything.

faqs.q: Why do you need my address and not just my phone number?
faqs.a: Because AC work is local. A condenser in League City is in salt air, one in Katy is under an oak tree dropping cottonwood, one in Bellaire has been sitting on a small lot since the 1950s. The company that covers your area will recognise the situation faster, and you are more likely to get someone who has seen your exact problem before.

faqs.q: How quickly will someone contact me?
faqs.a: That depends on the company that receives your request and on how urgent the problem is. If your system has gone down in the middle of a July week, say so in the description, because that changes how it gets handled. We make sure the request reaches a company that covers your street, but how quickly they call is their call to make.

faqs.q: Will I get a price before anyone comes out?
faqs.a: You should get a sense of cost before work begins, and you should ask for it. The cost depends on access, time of day, which part failed, and whether it is a repair or a replacement. Any company that will not talk about cost until the unit is already open should not be doing the job.

faqs.q: Are the companies you send me to licensed?
faqs.a: Every company we send work to holds a current Texas Air Conditioning Contractors license, and we check the license before the listing goes live. Ask for the license number on the call and look it up yourself in the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation register before work starts. A company with a real license will not mind you doing this.

faqs.q: My unit is running but the house is still hot. What should I do?
faqs.a: Do not keep lowering the thermostat. If the indoor coil has frozen, dropping the setting makes it worse. Turn the system off at the thermostat and let the coil thaw for a few hours, then try one cycle. If it happens again within a day, something mechanical is going on and it needs to be looked at.

faqs.q: What if my area is not listed on this site?
faqs.a: Request anyway. The list on this site shows where requests are actively being sent, and it is not the whole metro. If nobody covers your street, you will find out quickly and nothing is lost. If you are outside Greater Houston entirely, you are better off searching directly for a local company.
